subject: Recap & asks — Jupiter Health private deployment constraints and ops asks
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Alexandra Cheng <alex.cheng@jupiterhealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-21T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Recap & asks — Jupiter Health private deployment constraints and ops asks

Hi Alexandra — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side and a short list of asks so your infra/procurement teams can evaluate feasibility: 

Summary of what you shared
- Primary driver: regulatory requirement to keep PHI within US-resident infrastructure; production inference must be isolated (no public internet egress from inference nodes).
- Preference: on-prem air-gapped evaluation for pre-prod/dev; production can live in customer VPC w/ strict egress controls and dedicated subnets.
- Pain points: procurement lead time (SOC2 artifacts + PO timing), key management (HSM requirement), and tight change windows for inbound firewall modifications.

Open questions / asks (for your infra + procurement):
1) Can you confirm that "no internet egress" means absolutely no outbound connections from inference nodes except to an internal KMS endpoint we would configure? If there are allowed outbound destinations, please list IPs/FQDNs.
2) Will Jupiter allow VPC peering/PrivateLink to Redwood-hosted control plane, or do you require a full Private deployment inside your network?
3) Are health checks and metrics collection allowed to call back to a monitoring bucket (read-only) or do those need to land on a JumpBox?
4) Procurement: please share the PO/contract cadence and any required SOW language (cc'ing procurement/next email address is helpful).

Attachments: network-diagram.png (high-level), Redwood private deployment checklist (attached as PDF). These are intended to speed the infra scoping call.

Proposed next steps
- Share network diagram & checklist (attached) — done.
- Tech deep-dive with your infra + our infra leads: can we target Thu 2026-09-23 10:00-11:00 PT? Please confirm availability and preferred dial-in.
- Procurement intro: loop in procurement contact so we can share PO template and SOC2 artifacts.

If you prefer, I can put together a short feature/controls pack focused strictly on isolation and egress controls for your security team.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0182

From: Alexandra Cheng <alex.cheng@jupiterhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@jupiterhealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-22T09:16:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & asks — Jupiter Health private deployment constraints and ops asks

Thanks Jordan — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Egress constraints: for prod inference we require no outbound connections to the public internet from the inference subnet. Outbound to our internal KMS (10.12.24.10/32) and to our internal monitoring endpoint (10.12.24.20/32) is allowed.
2) Key management: we do require HSM-backed keys for any persistent model keys; for ephemeral session keys we can discuss a managed KMS integration.
3) Air-gap: dev and pre-prod must be physically air-gapped from the internet during the evaluation window. Production can be VPC-hosted with PrivateLink or peering as long as the peering is customer-initiated and we control route tables.

Procurement: I included procurement@jupiterhealth.com on this thread — they will pick this up for PO timelines. Attached is a very high-level infra PDF we shared internally (jupiter-infra-highlevel.pdf).

We can do Thu 2026-09-23 10:00 PT for the deep technical call — please send the calendar invite with dial-in.

Best,
Alexandra Cheng
Director, Infrastructure Security
Jupiter Health

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alexandra Cheng <alex.cheng@jupiterhealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-22T12:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & asks — Jupiter Health private deployment constraints and ops asks

Alexandra — appreciate the quick clarifications. A few technical items we want to confirm before the deep-dive so we can bring the right folks and diagrams: 

On Wed, Alexandra Cheng <alex.cheng@jupiterhealth.com> wrote:
> 1) Egress constraints: for prod inference we require no outbound connections to the public internet from the inference subnet. Outbound to our internal KMS (10.12.24.10/32) and to our internal monitoring endpoint (10.12.24.20/32) is allowed.

Our follow-ups / asks:
- IP ranges & allowed FQDNs: please confirm any CIDR ranges (we'll add to the checklist). If you prefer we can accept a signed network ACL export.
- Who will initiate peering? You noted customer-initiated peering — is that strictly required or can we provision PrivateLink and have you accept an endpoint?
- TLS & mTLS: do you require mutual TLS for control-plane connections, or is TLS1.2+ with client cert optional?
- Expected traffic profile: peak RPS and sustained concurrency (tokens/sec or requests/sec) — even rough numbers help sizing.
- Log retention & audit logs: duration required for access logs and whether logs must remain in your VPC (preferred) or can be archived to an encrypted bucket in our control plane.

Attachments: I'm re-attaching our Redwood private checklist to make the upcoming call efficient. If you can drop answers inline in the doc before the call, we can triage offline.

Proposed invite: Thu 2026-09-23 10:00 PT with Redwood Infra (network lead) + Solutions Eng + Jupiter infra/security + procurement. I'll send a calendar invite once I have confirmation.

Thanks — Lauren

From: Alexandra Cheng <alex.cheng@jupiterhealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@jupiterhealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-23T10:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & asks — Jupiter Health private deployment constraints and ops asks

Lauren / Jordan — quick answers inline to help you prepare for today's deep-dive: 

- IP ranges: prod monitoring & KMS endpoints are 10.12.24.10/32 and 10.12.24.20/32. If you need a CIDR for the inference subnet we can provide 10.12.40.0/24.
- Peering: customer must initiate peering and accept the connection; PrivateLink is acceptable but we prefer peering for lower ops overhead.
- TLS: mutual TLS is required for any control-plane connections (client certs).
- Traffic profile: initial pilot ~5 RPS (burst to 25 RPS). Production expected to be ~50 RPS with concurrency peaks for batch jobs; token throughput ~2k tokens/sec peak.
- Logs: access/audit logs must be stored in our encrypted S3 and retained for 7 years. We cannot allow long-term archival in an external control plane. Short-term read-only metrics can be polled via a push to our monitoring endpoint.

Procurement note: procurement@jupiterhealth.com, our target is to issue a PO by 2026-10-15 for a Q4 pilot. I'm attaching our PO template.

See you on the call.

—Alexandra
Alexandra Cheng
Director, Infrastructure Security | Jupiter Health
